# NOTES: *A TRAITOR'S WOOING* by Headon Hill (1909, Ward Lock; illustrated)

## BOOK 1 (main novel). Front matter / back matter are not story

**Front matter:** Title page. Blurbs for other Hill novels: *The Avengers*, *Millions of Mischief*, *Her Splendid Sin*, *Unmasked at Last*, *A Race with Ruin*, *The Hidden Victim*, *Radford Shone*. Contents list: 30 chapters (I Two Villains and the Heroine; II "A Screw Loose Somewhere"; III Presage of Storm; IV Nugent Moves a Pawn; V Under the Searchlight; VI The Cry from the Train; VII The Face in the Pool; VIII Intercepted; IX The Inquisitive Foreman; X The Lure of Love; XI The Peering Eyes; XII The *Cobra's* Sailing Orders; XIII Fool's Paradise Lost; XIV The Creaking Stair; XV A Council of Three; XVI Barbed Shafts; XVII "The Bootlace Man"; XVIII The Trap Is Set; XIX The Sleeping Snake; XX Blue Light and Green; XXI The Trap Closes; XXII The Shadow of Horror; XXIII In the Stone Grotto; XXIV In the Toils; XXV The Last Chance Fails; XXVI Enid Is "Mixed Up"; XXVII Pursuit; XXVIII Travers Nugent Pays; XXIX The Sting of the Nettle; XXX Aftermath of Storm).

**Back matter:** Ward, Lock & Co. catalogue of other novels and reviews (Weyman, Hope, Mason, Phillpotts, Doyle, Haggard, Crockett, Pemberton, Barr, Oppenheim, Innes, F.M. White, Forman, Bindloss, Tracy, Magnay, Hill, Boothby, Marchmont, Hocking, Moberly, Thorne, Eyre, Roberts, Leighton). Not part of story.

## CHARACTERS
- **Travers Nugent**: middle-aged, well-built, long fair moustache, close-set blue eyes, "shiftiness." Bachelor, no visible occupation, "lived on his wits." Jermyn Street flat; cottage **The Hut** on hill west of Ottermouth (butler Sinnett; chauffeur Dixon; later hangers-on Tuke). Income ~£100/yr from "avuncular oof-bird" uncle (died America); spends ~£2,000/yr. Drinks, cigars, orchids. Caresses moustache when thinking. Suave, cruel, cunning.
- **Bhagwan Singh, Maharajah of Sindkhote**: jewelled turban, pale olive skin, jet moustache, lazy cruel eyes. Rejected by Violet at Brabazon House ball ("laughed at me"). Plans abduction, "sweep out the harem." Offers Nugent £20,000. Buys Chermside's Indian debts as leverage.
- **Leslie Chermside**: tall, sun-browned, ex-officer 24th Lancers; ~2 years gap in record. Was commander of Maharajah's native bodyguard at Sindkhote; debts forced him to leave. Pledged to elope Violet. Falls genuinely in love with her; repents.
- **Violet Maynard**: tall, beautiful, daughter of Montague Maynard; "acknowledged beauty of the season"; artist's Academy picture; wears white.
- **Montague Maynard**: stout, florid, ~60, Birmingham screw-manufacturer (millionaire); villa at Harborne, Mercedes, Park Lane London house; rents **Ottermouth Manor** for summer. Blunt, jovial, "Vi" is his name for Violet. Widower.
- **Aunt Sarah Dymmock**: diminutive, severely dressed in black, lace cap, sunshade, wizened, sharp tongue, "Aunt Sally." Violet's mother's aunt; raised Violet; large fortune, "carefully-veiled kindness." Chases onion-seller off grounds.
- **Louise Aubin**: Violet's French maid (Normandy, from village of Dicamp; scrambled barefoot with Pierre as girl). Vain, greedy, coquettish, vindictive, "Mees" for Violet. Affair with Levison; later with Nugent.
- **Pierre Legros**: Breton onion-seller, sailor from French lugger (Captain Jules Epitaux) lying at Exmouth. Blue jean, barefoot, bloodshot eyes. Jealous lover of Louise. Kills Levison (confesses ch XXVIII).
- **Levi Levison** ("Levi/Levi Levison"): Jewish moneylender/"financial agent," Cockney, lisps, flashy dress, be-ringed hands, ~30. Stays at **Plume Hotel**. Nugent's tool. Murdered on marsh; throat cut and stabbed 3 times in back, once in chest.
- **Vernon Mallory**: retired Foreign Office man (40 years), ascetic, pale, sharp eyes, "noticed everything." Called "Vincent" once in error (ch IV). Wife **Margaret** blind. Daughter **Enid Mallory**: pert, "Pussy" nickname, golden hair, schoolgirl-turned-flirt, golf player; later engaged to Reggie.
- **Lieutenant Reginald "Reggie" Beauchamp**: RN, commands destroyer at Plymouth (*Snipe*, 30 knots); ~23 (later "eight-and-twenty"); cheerful. Mother **Mrs. Beauchamp**, widow of Admiral, Lorne Villas, Ottermouth. Gave Pussy nicknames.
- **General Kruse**: ex-Indian Staff Corps, big, rubicund, foghorn voice, "always full," nicknamed "the widow's Kruse."
- **Lazarus Lowch**: cadaverous, lantern-jawed, Mrs. Beauchamp's neighbour; spy-hole in privet hedge; loves funerals; always inquest foreman; widower. Engaged to Louise at end.
- **Sergeant Bruce**: local police sergeant, intelligent.
- **Dr.** (unnamed) and landlord of Plume (unnamed).
- **Captain Simon Brant**: of *Cobra*; tiny, pear-shaped cranium, yellow complexion, hopping gait, hissing breath, wolf-snarl laugh, Derringer. Sadistic.
- **Bully Cheeseman**: *Cobra's* bullet-headed mate; once suspected Jack the Ripper.
- **Wiley**: second mate, manslaughter record.
- **Rat Mullins**, **Snobby Wilson**: crew in launch. **Black Jake**: fireman shot/cremated in furnace.
- **Bill Tuke** ("The Bootlace Man"): raffish tramp; bootlace hawker disguise; bloated drinker face; Nugent's agent; locks Enid in grotto. Also was the "train man."
- **Nettle Jimpson**: tall, strong draper's assistant (Grigg & Winter/Wynter, Weymouth), 5ft 10, plain bold face, "stinging-nettle." Fiancé **Ned Parsons**, acting gunner (petty officer) on *Snipe*.
- **Second-Lieutenant Ellison** (lisp) on *Snipe*.
- **Enid's**: "Mona Dartring" (golf friend).
- **Watson**: Manor butler. **Dixon**: Nugent's chauffeur. **Sinnett**: Nugent's silent butler.

## PLACES
Ottermouth (South Devon resort; esplanade, parade, club at seaward end of main street, Plume Hotel, police station, coastguard station on Flagstaff Hill, marsh/old estuary east, pebble bank at river mouth, Manor House, The Hut, Lorne Villas). Exmouth (nearby; lugger). Portland, Weymouth (*Cobra* at quay). Plymouth/Devonport (Hamoaze, *Snipe*). Brixham trawlers, Berry Head. Sindkhote (Runn of Cutch, India). Brabazon House (London ball). Coldbrook/Colebrook Chine (landing point, beneath Nugent's cliff). Stone grotto at The Hut. Rose garden at Manor (sundial, box hedge, crimson rambler arch). Orangery (Manor).

## EVENTS, IN ORDER

**Ch I.** Brabazon House ball, London season. Nugent tells Maharajah Violet is alone; Maharajah walks with her to winter garden; returns furious; "She refused?" Brandy. Plan: Chermside as lover-bait; elope on fast steamer ("ostensibly his own yacht"); £20,000. Nugent: "Here is my hand on it... Your Highness has supplied the strategy; I will devise the tactics."

**Ch II.** August, noon, club. Mallory & Reggie at window. Steward: visitor (Levison) waiting at door; Chermside leaves with him toward marsh. Mallory: Chermside's Army record gap; "a steam yacht"; Maynard = "maker of screws in Birmingham." Reggie: "a loose screw somewhere." Marsh talk: Levison holds Chermside's debts; yacht at Portland with crew of fifty; Nugent arrived by late train; Levison's ultimatum; meet "ten o'clock to-morrow night" on marsh. Chermside's backstory: Maharajah's palace; sailed with letter to Nugent. Nugent rented Manor for Maynard via agent. Chermside now in love; resolves to refuse.

**Ch III.** Manor drive: Violet, Aunt Sarah, Chermside meets them; Aunt Sarah had chased onion-seller with sunshade. Aunt Sarah: "I wouldn't trust him [Nugent] with a shilling." Nugent arrives by car. Aunt Sarah: "as full of mischief as a ripe cheese is of maggots." Chermside tells Nugent: "I am not going on with the damned thing!" Lunch: Chermside plans anonymous warning to Maynard. Aunt Sarah: Louise was the onion-seller's former lover; the Plume visitor was her new admirer. Maynard recalls Maharajah's failed proposal; Nugent: Maharajah "left England within a few days of the ball." Violet: "I let him down easy last time."

**Ch IV.** Nugent's car; Enid grimaces at Reggie; Dixon names Reggie. The Hut: Sinnett. Nugent sends Sinnett to Exmouth for Pierre Legros ("I must have the man"). Levison in smoke-room: Chermside will refuse; Nugent: "turn the screw." Nugent asks about Louise (Levison's affair). Levison exits by moor gate.

**Ch V.** Reggie & Enid bicker; cruiser *Terrible* night practice. Date set: Reggie to Exeter next day; "prowl" that evening. Evening: they hide in "ambush" glade. Two men pass (first hurrying, puffing). Scream/wail from marsh. Searchlight from cruiser reveals Chermside on path. Enid: Chermside on a yacht "fitting out at Portland."

**Ch VI.** Club reading room: Nugent asks Chermside about Levison; Chermside rejects Maharajah's debts ("I owe him no allegiance whatever"). Kruse reports Levison missing from Plume. Nugent recommends picnic spot on marsh (sheltered 4 p.m.). Chermside pales. Picnic next day; ~100 guests; Nugent arrives in grey suit, orchid. Louise supervises. Train passes; passenger shouts (Reggie: "face of a fool"; Violet: "face in the pool").

**Ch VII.** Mallory finds body in pool under railway embankment. Maynard clears guests (Aunt Sarah manages). Police sergeant & doctor sent for. Reggie identifies Levison (remembers club window). Reggie: throat cut, not drowned. Reggie recalls scream.

**Ch VIII.** Louise intends to denounce Pierre; walks high road. Meets Nugent (tryst). Louise boasts she'll denounce Pierre Legros. Nugent denies Pierre's guilt (Pierre was at Nugent's back door at time of murder); hints at "a man who had an appointment on the marsh." Nugent gets Pierre's description. Nugent: "The treacherous little cat!"

**Ch IX.** Mrs. Beauchamp; Lowch spies through hedge. Reggie plans silence. Inquest at Plume long room: Lowch foreman. Witnesses: landlord; Chermside ("financial agent," business walk, not with Levison since previous day); Mallory; Dr. (multiple stabs, throat); Sgt. Bruce (body carried to pool). Lowch grills Reggie: heard scream; "thought it was a sea-bird, or possibly a snared rabbit." Adjourned. Mallory: "The boy is concealing something."

**Ch X.** Chermside's rooms; resolves to force Nugent's hand by staying with Violet. Rose garden with Violet: "I believe that your heart is in India." Violet: "I do not believe that you have done anything really base." Chermside: "it is your love I want, my darling." Embrace observed by Louise behind box hedge.

**Ch XI.** Louise deduces Chermside = Levison's appointment man. Visits Nugent at The Hut after dark (note via Sinnett). Nugent confirms (feigned reluctance) and reveals rose-garden kiss. Louise notices peering eyes at window; Nugent drags in Pierre. Louise & Pierre quarrel; Nugent threatens Pierre. Pierre reports an old bald gentleman with piercing eyes questioning him at Exmouth quay (Mallory). Pierre: "He will have to strike—always strike—if he is betrayed."

**Ch XII.** Ottermouth station, 9 a.m.: Nugent and Reggie. Nugent to Weymouth. At Weymouth: *Cobra* (2,000 ton turbine yacht, gilt lettering). Cheeseman blocks Nugent. Brant (captain) talks crew discipline; shot a man; "I'm the law on this ship." Signal plan: telegram "Advance"; steam west; abreast Ottermouth after sundown; lay to ≥3 miles; blue light then green half-mile west of town at foot of Coldbrook Chine; electric launch with three men.

**Ch XIII.** Chermside, Violet, Aunt Sarah plan sailing. Maynard dinner: asks Chermside's wealth; Chermside admits yacht not his; Maynard: "perfect frankness." Sail: Aunt Sarah: "You two are in love." Chermside confesses partial guilt (Maharajah plot). Aunt Sarah transfers securities ~£250,000 to Chermside ("I yesterday arranged..."). Nugent summons Chermside at club: "You will certainly be hanged."

**Ch XIV.** Card-room: Nugent: "under the gravest suspicion of having murdered Levi Levison." Nugent claims Louise (Levison's lover) threatens to tell police. Nugent proposes flight on *Cobra*, departure "day after to-morrow." Loose board creaks on stair. Billiard room: Mallory (vs Kruse, score 5-2), Lowch watching. Chermside wonders who overheard.

**Ch XV.** Mallory's house; Reggie and Enid announce engagement. Study: Mallory asks about marsh night; Reggie recounts; Enid notes Chermside wore flannels. Tramp with bootlaces at window; Enid identifies him as the train man. Reggie: he came from The Hut gates. Mallory: "find proof against the actual slayer." Reggie leaves for Plymouth next morning.

**Ch XVI.** Louise (coached by Nugent) confides to Violet that Chermside was Levison's appointment; Violet tells her to go to police. Dinner party at Manor (Mallorys, Chermside, Nugent, Aunt Sarah). Drawing room: Violet confronts Nugent; Nugent insinuates Chermside suspicious and says he suppressed Louise. Violet: "I am ashamed of you." Violet tells Nugent she advised maid to go to police. Orangery with Chermside: Violet: "Is that all you have to say to me?" She leaves him.

**Ch XVII.** Enid reads Reggie's letter (torpedo practice, leaving port 4 a.m.). Mallory: onion-seller/Louise lead; asks Enid to pump Louise. Enid at links with Mona Dartring; walks back past The Hut's oak back gate; enters garden; hides in shrubbery; sees Tuke (Bootlace Man) enter; hides in stone grotto; Tuke locks her in.

**Ch XVIII.** Nugent to Manor (Maynard in London). Tells Violet Chermside is fleeing to yacht tonight; police warrant; wants meeting before sailing. Sets meeting: 11 p.m., Ottermouth road near lodge, car waiting. Nugent: "In a little over four hours I shall have earned Bhagwan Singh's reward."

**Ch XIX.** *Cobra*: Brant reads letter; orders Cheeseman to buy women's clothes and hire stewardess. Cheeseman returns with Nettle Jimpson. Lazaretto cabin (iron ring, chain, leg-irons). Telegram "Advance" arrives; Brant burns it. *Cobra* leaves Weymouth, "sleeping snake." Nettle put in cabin; Brant promises a Plymouth stop (lie). Evening off Ottermouth; Brant orders Cheeseman, Rat Mullins, Snobby Wilson in launch.

**Ch XX.** Chermside at The Hut library; Nugent's lies (police warrant; Violet won't be told). Tuke returns, boasts of trapping "prisoner" in grotto (Enid). Nugent blusters (thinks Louise). Nugent gives flare signal instructions; leaves in car. Chermside and Tuke descend Colebrook (Coldbrook) Chine. Blue then green flares. Launch arrives.

**Ch XXI.** Aunt Sarah retires; Violet leaves via French window (Watson on alert). Nugent collects Violet by car (Dixon). Nugent's route through The Hut grounds; Violet hears something at grotto. At beach Tuke says Chermside boarded launch and left message: he'll ask captain to send launch back for Violet. Violet insists on going. Nugent: "The wait would be a long one." Nugent tells Tuke to release Enid and go to London. Nugent sees *Cobra* lights going west.

**Ch XXII.** Chermside on *Cobra*. Brant: second launch trip. Nettle (on deck) talks with Chermside: she was shipped as Violet's companion; assumes elopement. Violet's voice heard from launch; Chermside leaps into launch to stop abduction; fights crew, knocked down. Cheeseman's revolver: "I want him for something better."

**Ch XXIII.** Enid in grotto; discovers Pierre Legros under matting. Enid sympathizes (fiancé sailor "half dozen wives"). Pierre: Louise betrayed him; Nugent's jealousy; overheard "Jermicide" (Chermside) to be deported as decoy. Pierre removes slates from grotto roof using fertilizer kegs. Clock strikes 8, 9, 10, 11. Enid hears Violet's voice in garden, doesn't call out in time.

**Ch XXIV.** Violet boards *Cobra*; electric lights blaze. Brant: Sindkhote, "Runn of Cutch"; launch hoisted aboard; *Cobra* moves off. Brant reveals Maharajah's plot; Nugent engaged Brant. Chermside beaten, chained below. Violet meets Nettle: "I'm just as keen to get off it as you can be."

**Ch XXV.** Nettle & Violet ally; Violet: "Mr. Chermside is my lover." Nettle's plan: Plymouth letter to Ned (*Snipe*). Violet recalls *Snipe* = Reggie's ship. Sealed orders (text) reveal plan: Chermside as false flight, Maynard told he'll head to America, real course down-channel. Nettle goes to lower deck, finds Chermside chained; gives water. Dawn: Brant refuses Plymouth; "passed the opening of Plymouth Sound an hour ago." "Our last chance had failed."

**Ch XXVI.** Mallory at club (Thursday bridge); Lowch confronts: watched Enid go into Nugent's garden (Enid appears, bramble-scratched, golf skirt torn). Mallory's analysis: Violet decoyed to steamer bound for India by Bhagwan Singh. Telephone exchange (closed 8 p.m.; bribed). Enid: "Come along and see."

**Ch XXVII.** Reggie at Devonport mess; 12:30 a.m. phone call from Enid (exchange lady). Reggie decides to intercept; crew: Second-Lt. Ellison, acting gunner Ned Parsons. *Snipe* leaves Plymouth Sound; passes *Cobra* in the dark; Parsons recognizes Nettle on deck. *Cobra* speeds up (40 knots) and escapes.

**Ch XXVIII.** Nugent returns from The Hut grotto (Enid gone, roof hole). Nugent's musings (Chermside lost, Louise to be dismissed by palm-grease, Pierre risk). Mallory, Sgt. Bruce arrive 12:30 a.m. Mallory: "I charge you... as an accessory before the fact" to Levison's murder. Pierre (behind screen) confesses killing Levison at Nugent's instigation (time/place arranged). Nugent pretends to fetch bag; reaches for revolner; Pierre stabs Nugent in neck with sheath knife; Pierre stabs himself to death.

**Ch XXIX.** *Cobra* sighted; Brant's false terror routine. Nettle to skylight over engine-room; Cheeseman fires at her; bullet glances off bucket; Nettle dumps cinders into machinery; engines wrecked.

**Ch XXX.** Engines stopped; Brant threatens Nettle with Derringer ("Will you jump overboard yourself, or shall I shoot you first?"). Nettle: Ned will board. Brant throws Derringer over. *Snipe* swoops down. Coda (Manor dinner, a few days later): Maynard, Mallory, Reggie. Chermside confessed to Mallory that morning; Mallory advised him; Maynard accepts him. Reggie: Maynard bought Grigg & Wynter (sic) for Nettle as reward. Mallory's account: Nugent planned Levison murder to scare Chermside. Louise Aubin to marry Lowch ("figures in old Lowch's pass-book"). Aunt Sarah & Enid tell grotto story to Violet. END.

## INCONSISTENCIES IN TEXT (as printed)
- Mallory's first name: "Vernon" (most) vs "Vincent" (ch IV).
- "Coldbrook" Chine (ch XII, XX) vs "Colebrook" (ch XXI, XXIV).
- Draper's firm: "Grigg and Winter" vs "Grigg and Wynter" (ch XXX).
- Pierre names Chermside "Jermicide."
- Tide/moon/timing details vary slightly by chapter.
- Enid's grotto escape: Pierre's roof hole, but Enid's "ten o'clock" vs "eleven" references.
